Bidirectional Mendelian randomization uses genetically predicted 25-hydroxyvitamin D and Parkinson case-status datasets. Its null causal estimates concern genetically proxied vitamin D and disease risk, without a fig intake or symptom contrast.
The study docks diterpenoid structures from Xylopia aethiopica against MAO-B and compares simulated binding. Its computational compound ranking supplies no actual feeding or rest-tremor measurement.

The review surveys central cholinergic evidence across Parkinson motor and nonmotor signs and distinguishes resting from action tremor. The relevant mechanisms and interventions contain no isolated fig exposure or intake-linked effect.

The clinical biospecimen study measures alpha-synuclein misfolding in cerebrospinal fluid using immuno-infrared sensing. Its signal and diagnostic-cohort differences concern misfolding classification, without a dietary fig analysis.

The original study integrates public expression and immune gene datasets and uses feature selection to identify inflammatory biomarker candidates. Its outcomes are classifiers and candidate genes, with no raw fig exposure or clinical resting-tremor comparison.

Public expression data and defined ferroptosis or stress-related genes inform a computational biomarker pipeline. Reported gene networks and diagnostic markers do not compare fig consumption or resting tremor.

This review describes a literature search on T-cell involvement in Parkinson disease and discusses evidence of CNS infiltration and treatment hypotheses. The clinical and mechanistic sources provide no raw fig exposure comparison.

The animal cohorts monitor total feed and water and compare stool measures by sex and c-Rel genotype alongside other tests. Food measurement is undifferentiated, and the body supplies no fig analysis or patient rest-tremor outcome.

The computational model changes basal-ganglia stimulation and synaptic parameters. Its measured endpoint is simulated beta power suppression, without food assignment or patient resting-tremor severity.

The experimental study prepares a methanolic leaf extract of Acacia jacquemontii and assesses toxicity-model animal behaviors, including beam walking. It distinguishes the botanical source and processed extract, with no raw fig or Parkinson patient rest-tremor contrast.

This comprehensive review describes Parkinson motor signs and dopaminergic neuron degeneration, then synthesizes cellular mechanisms and pathways. It supplies no defined raw fig comparison or intake-related resting tremor.

The clinical study deploys a tablet cognitive battery in people with Parkinson disease and analyzes test completion and cognitive structure. The described clinical signs do not turn this into a fig exposure or resting-tremor study.

The preclinical report evaluates a targeted SNCA transcriptional repression strategy in laboratory and mouse models. The efficacy readouts concern molecular suppression and animal movement, with no raw fig exposure or patient outcome.

The study compares public kidney and Parkinson transcriptomic cohorts and applies cohort-wise multiple-test control to cross-disease signals. It measures transcriptional overlap, with no food or resting-tremor outcome.

The exploratory plasma-metabolomics study integrates candidate signals with Mendelian randomization for Parkinson risk. Lifestyle and dietary granularity are limited and the conclusions do not provide an individual fig or resting-tremor contrast.

The prospective movement study measures directional body-segment coupling during gait and relates kinematic factors to diagnosis and motor severity. Its locomotor comparison does not isolate fig intake or a resting-tremor effect.

The study combines repository transcriptomic sets and machine learning to classify Parkinson-related mitochondrial dynamics markers. The biomarker estimates furnish no fig intake or separately tested clinical resting-tremor comparison.

The BioFIND biospecimen study compares two alpha-synuclein aggregation assays in Parkinson and control CSF. Clinical assessments and sampling conditions are separate from its assay agreement outcomes, with no fig exposure.

The clinical imaging study compares degenerative parkinsonian subtypes and tracer-uptake indices with support-vector machine classification. It uses diagnostic groups, without a food-related rest-tremor comparison.

The newly diagnosed Parkinson cohort collects clinical histories and diagnostic timing. Rest tremor is one onset phenotype in the diagnostic-latency curves, with no fig intake variable or fig-linked severity result.

The imaging cohort measures retinal layers with optical coherence tomography in de novo Parkinson and controls and examines cognitive correlates. Rest tremor helps define clinical eligibility, and the results do not test fig.

This post hoc analysis follows safinamide versus placebo in an extension trial and reports OFF/ON time and other Parkinson measures. The randomized exposure is a drug and the analysis contains no fig intake comparison.

The randomized feasibility study compares Leap Motion serious games with conventional upper-limb rehabilitation. Grip and dexterity outcomes concern task-based rehabilitation, without an oral fig exposure.

The PRECODE-1 analysis follows early Parkinson participants to predict cognitive decline using clinical markers. Resting tremor contributes to entry phenotype and the analyses provide no fig-based outcome.

The experimental task studies implicit switching in medicated Parkinson patients. Its behavioral results address task responses and completion, without food intake or a fig-based rest-tremor contrast.

The INVEST protocol compares intrajejunal levodopa infusion with deep brain stimulation and specifies follow-up outcomes. This is a treatment protocol, and the intestinal delivery route supplies no culinary fig arm or result.

The obstacle-crossing experiment uses UPDRS motor items including rest and action tremor to designate the more affected side. Its reported outcomes concern foot clearance and gait asymmetry, without a fig exposure.

The modeling study fits motor response data to levodopa pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics using clinical ratings. Its modeled treatment is levodopa, with no fig predictor or food-related resting-tremor measure.
The postmortem study follows prior neurturin gene therapy, examining brain expression and tissue pathology. Rest tremor frames the disease history, without a food intervention or fig-linked outcome.

The smart-device experiment compares visuomotor adaptation in medicated Parkinson patients and controls. Resting tremor is among diagnostic features, and the tablet adaptation outcomes provide no fig exposure.

The cohort records free-living gait with a waist-mounted sensor and relates gait acceleration to cognition and motor scores. Its movement measures contain no individual fig intake or fig-linked resting-tremor comparison.

The focused-ultrasound thalamotomy series records MRI lesions and clinical tremor signs, with one Parkinson participant in a mostly essential-tremor sample. Its case-level tremor outcomes apply to the procedure without fig exposure.
The DBS study changes current steering across electrode contacts and records gait and stimulation energy. The setting comparison and reported motor performance have no fig intake component.

The neurofilament light assay uses clinical definitions including resting tremor in Parkinson or Parkinson dementia enrollment. The laboratory outcome concerns assay performance, without a fig consumption or rest-tremor comparison.
The observational smartphone study measures inertial features during a 20-step walking test and classifies Parkinson status. Its selected walking features provide no fig exposure measure.

The perioperative randomized study compares inhalational and intravenous anesthesia in people undergoing cerebral stimulator implantation. Its results track inflammatory cytokines, without a food or fig-linked tremor comparison.

The intervention study contrasts Brazilian rhythmic dance with walking sessions and evaluates mobility and gait before and after training. The measured movement changes concern exercise type, with no fig assignment.

The accelerometry pilot combines activity epochs and clinical resting-tremor information to classify movement and medication states during hospitalization. The analytic outcomes do not link fig consumption to resting tremor.

The primary Rotterdam Study cohort compares orthostatic blood-pressure change with prevalent and incident Parkinson disease. Orthostatic hypotension was associated with prevalent disease and did not confer higher incident risk in the reported follow-up. There is no fig intake comparison or separate resting-tremor effect by food exposure.

The study cultures patient-derived neural cells characterized by a VPS35 variant and examines endosomal and related cell measures. Its genetic and in vitro contrasts furnish no fig or patient resting-tremor outcome.

The SYNAPSES observational cohort follows patients prescribed safinamide in routine care and reports adverse events and clinical outcomes. Its exposure is a prescribed drug, with nutrition only an adverse-event category and no fig intake comparison.

The retrospective case series reviews surgical fixation of upper-extremity fractures in people with Parkinson disease. The outcomes are healing and surgery-related complications, without dietary fig exposure or linked resting tremor.

The nonhuman primate study compares intranasal experimental alpha-synuclein fibrils with controls and measures microglial and nigrostriatal iron effects. It has no ingestion or fig-linked clinical tremor outcome.

The pharmacology study screens selective tryptophan dioxygenase inhibitors and examines model targets and movements. Its compound and model comparisons do not administer raw fig or measure clinical rest tremor.

The cross-sectional quality-of-life analysis compares people with and without OFF episodes. Difficulty cutting food is a functional questionnaire item, without specific food intake or a fig-linked resting-tremor result.

The blinded-assessor trial assigns Parkinson patients with anxiety to cognitive behavioral therapy plus monitoring or monitoring alone. Its anxiety scale comparisons give no fig intake or a food-based tremor result.
The retrospective clinical series examines urodynamic obstruction in men with Parkinson disease. Resting tremor occurs in one diagnostic history, while the urinary comparisons have no fig exposure.

The nationwide claims study compares aspiration pneumonia and mortality in incident Parkinson patients and matched controls. Neurological diagnostic criteria do not provide specific fig exposure or Parkinson resting-tremor effects by food.

The imaging study compares MRI microbleeds, plasma amyloid and cognitive outcomes in Parkinson and controls. Clinical disease context includes resting tremor and the reported imaging comparisons lack fig exposure.
The device study records resting hand and forearm movements and evaluates diagnostic classification, with clinical UPDRS item 20 as a tremor descriptor. Its sensor findings do not compare fig intake.
The randomized sham crossover pilot applies anodal cerebellar stimulation and compares emotion recognition. Its motor-background language and cognitive outcomes have no raw fig exposure.

The PPMI analysis compares cerebral atrophy and cognitive performance by sex and probable REM sleep behavior disorder. Fruit and vegetable naming belongs to a semantic fluency assessment, with no fruit ingestion or fig-related resting-tremor result.

The randomized stimulation-frequency crossover records walking rhythmicity and explicitly describes worsened resting tremor under low-frequency stimulation for ten participants. The effect is tied to DBS settings, without a fig exposure.

The prediction study uses Medicare claims from defined cases and controls to compare models identifying prodromal Parkinson disease. The prediction outcomes do not assess raw fig or resting-tremor severity.
The primary EEG study compares network synchronization patterns by freezing-of-gait status. Its relevant findings concern brain signals and gait classification, without fig intake measurements.

The untreated Parkinson cohort and controls undergo repeated immune-cell characterization in a two-year follow-up study. Its results address immune populations and clinical traits without a fig exposure comparison.

The PPMI study quantifies cerebrospinal glucosylceramide across GBA-associated and idiopathic Parkinson disease. Rest tremor forms part of participant eligibility, without fig intake or an intake-linked severity result.

The SPARK screening analysis evaluates dopamine-transporter imaging to enrich a phase 2 antibody trial. Maximum UPDRS resting tremor describes stratified screening groups, without fig intake or a dietary trial.
